description.p: Open your Markdown files for beautiful, distraction-free reading with syntax-highlighted code blocks, tables, task lists, and clickable links. When you need to edit, switch to a comfortable editor with live preview.

Manuscript renders Markdown natively without a web engine, resulting in instant startup and low memory usage. It follows your system theme automatically and adapts to any screen size, from phones to desktops.

ul.li: Three view modes: Read, Edit, and Split with live preview
Tables rendered as a grid with borders, header row and inline formatting
Customizable font, spacing, and content width
Recent files, drag and drop, printing

description.p: Selecting text inside a table taller than the window no longer scrolls back to the table's first row. Adds a Support Development link (Ko-fi). Thanks to Russell Haley for two detailed reviews.

Large documents open several times faster and use far less memory: the rendered view draws only what is on screen, and tables are built as you scroll to them. A 1 MB file with hundreds of tables now shows in about 4 seconds instead of 10, using about 90 MiB instead of 540 MiB.
Navigation, copying and speed.

ul.li: Back / forward history across files, wikilinks and outline jumps (header arrows, Alt+Left/Right, mouse side buttons); every file remembers its own scroll position
Copying several lines or a table from the rendered view yields Markdown that pastes intact into another file
Search finds text inside table cells
Images inside HTML blocks (GitHub README style) are shown, side by side
Single newlines join into flowing paragraphs, as on GitHub (optional); numbered lists show numbers; horizontal rules and list spacing fixed
Automatic reload now works with editors that save atomically
Faster re-rendering: images are decoded once at display size and cached, syntax highlighting is cached, the spell checker loads only when enabled
Fixed a jump to the top when clicking into the text, and files being marked modified when switching to Edit
New File button in the header

description.p: Rich tables are now on by default — tables render as a grid with borders, a styled header row and inline formatting; plain-text tables remain available in Preferences → Writer. Split view keeps the preview aligned with the editor block by block instead of by a whole-document ratio, and double-clicking the divider resets the panes to equal halves. A table no longer stops the divider from narrowing the preview, the header shows the real folder of files opened through the file chooser, and the open-folder button stays visible when the file tree is hidden.

Adaptive-layout fixes for narrow windows. Both sidebars — the left file tree and the right outline — now overlay the content on narrow windows instead of squeezing it, and dock beside it when there is room; the header drops its stats label, title and view-mode toggles (still reachable from the menu) only when the window is genuinely narrow. The vault sidebar's collapsed state is remembered across launches, and content width 0 (unlimited) no longer breaks the layout on narrow windows.

Vault sidebar and working wikilinks. A left-hand file tree shows the current folder (or an explicitly opened vault) — directories expand lazily, a single click opens a Markdown file, and the sidebar docks beside the content on desktop widths while overlaying on narrow screens. Clicking a [[wikilink]] navigates to the matching note, creating it if it does not exist yet; targets are contained to the vault. Setting content width to 0 (unlimited) no longer clamps the view to the window width on startup.

Optional footer with word count, reading time and a daily word goal tracker — the goal icon flips from outline to filled once today's count meets the goal, and a writing-stats dialog is reachable from the hamburger menu. PDF / print export repeats the table header row on every continuation page when a table is split, with an orphan-header guard. Rich-table cells now respond to link clicks and the grid reflows to the TextView width on resize. Keyboard scrolling in View mode (Up/Down/PgUp/PgDn/Home/End/Space). Inter font is shipped inside the Flatpak so the configured default resolves inside the sandbox.

Rich tables — tables now render as embedded GtkGrid widgets with cell borders, header styling, alternating-row backgrounds and inline formatting inside cells (opt-in via Preferences → Writer). PDF and print export draws tables directly via cairo for proper borders, header backgrounds and clean row pagination across page breaks.

Export, search, and editing-flow update. The File menu gains an Export as PDF… action that uses the same Pango layout engine as printing, producing an A4 PDF without an external pandoc / LaTeX dependency. Font family and page margins are configurable in Preferences. Page breaks now clip to the bottom of the last fully fitted line, so a line that overflows starts cleanly on the next page instead of being cut in half.

Remote images referenced with ![alt](https://…) now actually render: bytes are fetched asynchronously, decoded in-process, cached in memory by URL, and applied to a placeholder Picture once the download completes.
The search bar shows a live X / Y match counter; the currently focused match renders in green while the other matches stay yellow. Match highlighting clears automatically when the search bar closes.

An optional Auto-save toggle in Preferences writes the current file roughly a second and a half after the last edit; the file-watch reload toast is suppressed during the self-write. A new Quick Open dialog (Ctrl+Shift+O) fuzzy-matches against recent files and markdown siblings of the current document. The default editor font is now Inter, with a graceful fall back to the system sans serif on systems where Inter is not installed.

Visual + performance update. Headings get a graduated blue accent per level (H1 → H6) and a more dramatic scale jump. GitHub-style callouts > [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!WARNING], [!DANGER], [!IMPORTANT] render as coloured blocks with an icon and bold title; custom titles are supported. Obsidian-style wikilinks [[name]] / [[name|label]] render in a violet accent (vault navigation is a future feature; clicks are captured locally). Embedded images now have rounded corners and always display at a sensible size. Blockquotes get a soft background tint, task markers switch to filled / empty discs, and inline code uses a warmer amber palette. The outline panel always overlays the content instead of pushing it sideways. Performance: focus mode caches the current paragraph and only re-applies the dim tag when the cursor leaves it, typewriter scroll and resize margin recomputation are coalesced through a stored idle, identical font-CSS reloads are skipped, and refresh_view / refresh_split_render now hash-skip when content and theme haven't changed.

First stable release. Distraction-free fullscreen (F11, hides chrome and scrollbars), Focus mode (dim text outside the current paragraph) and Typewriter mode (current line pinned to viewport center, half-viewport overscroll added so centering works at the document edges), all toggleable from a new Writer group in Preferences. Print is rewritten: it now prints the rendered markdown — headings keep their size and weight, code blocks keep their shading, lists keep their bullets, tables render as a box-drawing grid. Mobile UX: edge-swipe to open the outline, a bottom action bar with formatting shortcuts (visible on narrow screens while a source view has focus), and horizontal swipe toggles Read and Edit. Split mode now scrolls the rendered pane proportionally to the cursor in the source pane. Inline HTML fragments (such as
) are now rendered instead of silently dropped.

Adds Find and Replace (Ctrl+H) with a Replace All button and a green flash on the replaced text, explicit previous / next match buttons in the search bar, inline spell check (toggleable in Preferences, language picker populated from installed dictionaries), and multi-instance file opening so two documents tile side by side. Fixes the Ctrl shortcuts on non-Latin keyboard layouts (Russian, etc.), the outline panel click actually scrolling the view in all three modes, and the search jump landing on the right match in read mode.

Fixes YAML frontmatter being rendered as a thematic break, removes the heading underline that used to wrap into a thick band on narrow windows, and eliminates the last reference cycle keeping windows alive after close. Adds footnotes: [^a] references render as small superscript numbers and definitions appear in a dim style at the bottom.

Adds an outline sidebar (F9) for jumping between headings, smart list continuation, Ctrl+N for a new untitled document, and Ctrl+W to close the current file. Last open file, view mode and scroll position are now restored on launch (toggle in Preferences). Headings with inline code are tagged correctly, fixing the outline and improving rendering.

Adds word count and reading time in the header bar, session zoom (Ctrl+=, Ctrl+-, Ctrl+0), and Markdown editing shortcuts (Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+K). External file changes now offer a Reload toast instead of overwriting unsaved edits. Tables align correctly with emoji and CJK content, and adjacent lists no longer get a doubled gap.
Fixes full-text search on Cyrillic and emoji text, plugs a tag table leak on file auto-reload, and corrects the "0 = unlimited" content width option. CLI no longer panics on remote URIs.

Major rendering improvements: blank lines from source are now preserved, paragraphs with only bold or inline content no longer merge, and nested lists render correctly. About dialog now adapts to mobile screens.
Fixed table column alignment. Updated icon with proper padding and new screenshots.
Fixed tables with links and formatted text inside cells. Preferences dialog now has a close button on mobile. Upgraded to libadwaita 1.5.
Redesigned app icon to follow GNOME HIG guidelines. Updated screenshots to correct resolution.
Improved Flathub metadata: rewritten app description, simplified desktop categories, updated branding colors, and pinned screenshot URLs to version tags.

Polished rendering with larger headings, underline separators, and better code block styling. Inline formatting now works correctly inside lists. Added content width setting, Ctrl+Y redo, and unlimited undo.

Initial release with Markdown rendering, syntax-highlighted code blocks, three view modes (Read, Edit, Split), full-text search, file watching, customizable appearance, and adaptive layout for mobile.
